fullPassage:
Wheels of Adventures

A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn't sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but Dan assured me that we would be the coolest travelers in Northern California. When we finally landed in San Francisco, the Golden Gate City, Dan shouted, "Let's get rolling!"

Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us aboard, and we were off.

Fisherman's Wharf is popular for its pretty shops and seafood restaurants. We were hungry, but it took almost an hour for us to look around and decide what to eat for lunch. We chose to eat a roasted crab and clam chowder soup. The sea lions peacefully lying on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate. They didn't smell pleasant up close, yet their cuteness delayed our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge, the famous spot that appears in most movies and TV shows filmed in San Francisco. We took a cruise, enjoying the view of the city. As we passed the bridge, the summer breeze blew slowly, and we watched the beautiful sunset.

The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco and about five times bigger than Seoul. The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. Dan's uncle Roy, who lives in San Francisco, kindly gave us a ride to the park. While heading east in his car, we saw the scenery gradually changing from city to suburb, to forest, and finally, to mountain. By lunchtime, we arrived at the park, and each of us had a giant hamburger to fuel up for a hike.

While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped frequently to appreciate the fresh air blowing through the giant sequoias. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, which is about 63.7 meters tall and is almost 3,000 years old. It was massive, and I felt quite small in comparison.

Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to approach us. Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, yelling and waving. After turning me around, Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came. Dan said, "I guess it's time to leave now." That wasn't a problem because I had gotten my picture!

Another memorable part of the trip was the bike ride. Dan found out that the National Park has a bike rental service and offers hand-crank bikes. Dan persuaded me to try one, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park. The Tunnel View in Yosemite Valley was like a masterpiece painted by Mother Nature. The trail also led us to green fields and streams where we saw some wildlife. Watching people floating down the Merced River and hiking the Half Dome was cool. It was indeed a wonderful trip, with lots of laughter, joy, and sweat.

I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, including one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was fortunate to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was courage. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.

questions.passage: A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, ①<u>feeling</u> excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn't sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but Dan ②<u>assured</u> me that we would be the coolest travelers in Northern California. When we finally ③<u>landed</u> in San Francisco, the Golden Gate City, Dan shouted, "Let's get ④<u>roll</u>!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Dan이 "출발하자!"라고 외쳤다. 'get rolling'이 올바른 표현이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ roll → rolling: 'get + ~ing'는 '~하기 시작하다'의 관용 표현. Let's get rolling = 출발하자
❌ ① feeling: 분사구문으로 주어(I)의 감정을 설명. 정상
❌ ② assured: 'assure + 목적어 + that절' 구조. 정상
❌ ③ landed: 과거시제, 시간 부사절 when과 함께 사용. 정상
det.tip: get + ~ing: 시작하다. get rolling(출발하다), get going(움직이다). get + p.p.(수동)와 혼동 주의

questions.passage: Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, ①<u>which</u> I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and I ②<u>got on</u> the bus, the friendly driver ③<u>welcomed</u> us aboard, and we ④<u>was</u> off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Dan과 내가 버스에 타자 친절한 운전사가 우리를 환영했고, 우리는 출발했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ was → were: 주어가 'we'(복수)이므로 be동사는 were가 맞음
❌ ① which: 관계대명사 계속적 용법, 선행사 cable cars. 정상
❌ ② got on: 'get on the bus' 버스에 타다. 정상
❌ ③ welcomed: 'welcome + 목적어 + aboard' 구조. 정상
det.tip: 주어-동사 수일치: we → were. 'we were off' = 우리는 출발했다

questions.passage: The sea lions peacefully ①<u>lying</u> on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate. They didn't smell ②<u>pleasant</u> up close, yet their cuteness delayed our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge, the famous spot ③<u>that</u> appears in most movies and TV shows ④<u>filming</u> in San Francisco.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 샌프란시스코에서 촬영된(filmed) 영화와 TV 프로그램에 등장하는 유명한 장소.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ filming → filmed: 영화가 '촬영하는' 것이 아니라 '촬영된' 것이므로 과거분사 필요
❌ ① lying: 현재분사, sea lions를 수식. '누워있는 바다사자들'. 정상
❌ ② pleasant: 감각동사 smell 뒤 형용사 보어. 정상
❌ ③ that: 관계대명사 주격, 선행사 the famous spot. 정상
det.tip: 현재분사(-ing) vs 과거분사(-ed): movies filmed(촬영된 영화) — 영화는 촬영 '되는' 것이므로 수동(p.p.)

questions.passage: It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to approach us. ①<u>Thinking</u> quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, ②<u>yelling</u> and waving. After ③<u>turning</u> me around, Dan helped Uncle Roy ④<u>to push</u> me back the way we came.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Dan은 Roy 삼촌이 나를 밀어서 되돌아가도록 도왔다(helped push).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ to push → push: help + 목적어 + 동사원형(원형부정사). 'helped Uncle Roy push'가 올바름
❌ ① Thinking: 분사구문, Uncle Roy가 빠르게 생각하며. 정상
❌ ② yelling: 동시동작을 나타내는 분사. 돌을 던지며 소리 지르며. 정상
❌ ③ turning: 전치사 after + 동명사. 나를 돌린 후에. 정상
det.tip: help + 목적어 + 동사원형/to부정사: 둘 다 가능하지만, 원문은 'helped Uncle Roy push'로 원형부정사 사용. 시험에서는 help 뒤 to부정사/원형 구분 빈출

questions.passage: The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. Dan's uncle Roy, who lives in San Francisco, kindly gave us a ride to the park. While heading east in his car, we saw the scenery gradually changing from city to suburb, to forest, and finally, to mountain. By lunchtime, we arrived at the park, and each of us had a giant hamburger to ①<u>fuel up</u> for a hike. While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped ②<u>frequently</u> to appreciate the fresh air blowing through the giant sequoias. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, which is about 63.7 meters tall and is almost 3,000 years old. It was ③<u>massive</u>, and I felt quite ④<u>grand</u> in comparison.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 그것은 거대했고, 비교하면 나는 꽤 작게(small) 느껴졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ grand(웅장한) → small(작은): 거대한 나무와 비교하여 '작게' 느꼈다는 맥락에서 grand는 반대
❌ ① fuel up(에너지 보충): 하이킹을 위해 먹었다는 원문 그대로
❌ ② frequently(자주): 세쿼이아를 감상하려고 자주 멈췄다는 원문 그대로
❌ ③ massive(거대한): 63.7m 나무에 대한 묘사로 원문 그대로
det.tip: small(작은) ↔ grand(웅장한). in comparison(비교하면)이 핵심 단서

questions.passage: I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, including one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have ①<u>valuable</u> memories too. I was ②<u>fortunate</u> to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to ③<u>overcome</u> and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was ④<u>caution</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 내가 가져가야 할 전부는 용기(courage)뿐이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ caution(주의, 조심) → courage(용기): 장애물을 극복하고 새 세계로 뛰어들었다는 맥락에서 '조심'이 아닌 '용기'가 적합
❌ ① valuable(가치 있는): 소중한 추억이라는 원문 그대로
❌ ② fortunate(다행인): 좋은 동행에 대한 감사. 원문 그대로
❌ ③ overcome(극복하다): 장애물을 극복하다. 원문 그대로
det.tip: courage(용기) ↔ caution(조심). 글의 메시지는 '새로운 도전에 용기를 갖자'이므로 caution은 부적절

questions.passage: A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"글쓴이는 부모님과 함께 샌프란시스코로 여행을 갔다."

det.korean: 부모님 없이(without my parents) 여행했다고 했으므로 일치하지 않는다.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 'traveling without my parents'(부모님 없이 여행)이므로 부모님과 함께 갔다는 진술은 거짓
❌ T: 원문과 반대 내용
det.tip: without(~없이) 키워드를 놓치면 오답. 부정어 포함 여부를 꼼꼼히 확인

questions.passage: While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped frequently to appreciate the fresh air blowing through the giant sequoias. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, which is about 63.7 meters tall and is almost 3,000 years old.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"그리즐리 자이언트(Grizzly Giant)는 약 63.7미터 높이의 나무로 약 3,000년이 되었다."

det.korean: 그리즐리 자이언트는 약 63.7미터(63.7 meters) 높이이고 거의 3,000년(3,000 years)이 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ T: '63.7 meters tall'과 'almost 3,000 years old'로 원문 내용과 일치
❌ F: 수치가 원문과 정확히 일치
det.tip: 숫자와 단위를 정확히 확인. about/almost는 '약/거의'의 의미

questions.passage: Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to approach us.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"글쓴이는 곰을 만나자 두려워서 도망쳤다."

det.korean: 글쓴이는 곰을 보고 너무 신나서(so excited) 카메라를 꺼내 사진을 찍었다.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 'so excited that I took out my camera'이므로 두려워하지 않고 오히려 흥분했음
❌ T: 원문과 반대. 도망친 것이 아니라 사진을 찍으려 했음
det.tip: 감정 표현 주의: excited(흥분한) ≠ scared/frightened(두려운). 패러프레이징된 진술의 감정 단어를 꼼꼼히 확인

questions.passage: Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take __________. When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us aboard, and we were off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: a city tour bus with wheelchair access

det.korean: 케이블카가 휠체어를 수용하지 않으므로, 휠체어 접근이 가능한 시티투어 버스(a city tour bus with wheelchair access)를 타기로 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ a city tour bus with wheelchair access: 케이블카 대안으로 휠체어 접근 가능한 버스를 선택. 뒤 문장 'got on the bus'가 단서
❌ ① a taxi to the airport: 공항으로 간다는 내용 없음
❌ ② the cable car downtown: 바로 앞에서 케이블카가 휠체어 불가라고 했음
❌ ④ a ferry across the bay: 페리 이야기는 등장하지 않음
det.tip: 'Therefore(그러므로)'가 인과 관계 단서. 문제(케이블카 불가) → 해결(버스 선택)

questions.passage: I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was fortunate to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was __________. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 내가 가져가야 할 전부는 용기(courage)뿐이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① courage(용기): 장애물 극복, 새 세계 도전의 맥락에서 '용기'가 핵심 메시지
❌ ② patience(인내): 도전을 직면하는 맥락에서 '인내'보다 '용기'가 더 적합
❌ ③ money(돈): 교훈적 결말에 물질적 요소 부적합
❌ ④ luck(행운): 스스로 도전한 것이므로 행운이 아닌 용기
det.tip: 글의 주제: 도전과 용기. 'dove into a new world'(새 세계로 뛰어들다)가 핵심 단서

questions.passage: The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco and about five times bigger than Seoul. The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. Dan's uncle Roy, who lives in San Francisco, kindly gave us a ride to the park.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 요세미티 국립공원은 샌프란시스코에서 두 시간 거리에 있다.
요세미티 국립공원은 서울의 약 다섯 배 크기이다.
Dan의 삼촌 Roy는 요세미티에 살고 있다.

det.korean: 요세미티는 샌프란시스코에서 4시간(four hours) 거리이고 서울의 약 5배(five times) 크기이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 서울의 약 다섯 배: 'about five times bigger than Seoul' 원문과 일치
❌ ① 두 시간: 'four hours away'이므로 4시간
❌ ③ 요세미티에 산다: 'who lives in San Francisco'이므로 샌프란시스코 거주
❌ ④ 기차: 'gave us a ride'(차로 데려다 주었다)이므로 자동차
det.tip: 숫자 변조(4시간→2시간)와 장소 변조(샌프란시스코→요세미티)가 오답 함정

questions.passage: Dan found out that the National Park has a bike rental service and offers hand-crank bikes. Dan persuaded me to try one, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park. The Tunnel View in Yosemite Valley was like a masterpiece painted by Mother Nature. The trail also led us to green fields and streams where we saw some wildlife.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Dan이 글쓴이에게 핸드크랭크 자전거를 타보라고 설득했다.
글쓴이는 핸드크랭크 자전거를 잘 타지 못했다.
터널 뷰는 자연이 그린 걸작 같았다.

det.korean: 글쓴이는 곧 핸드크랭크를 꽤 잘(pretty well) 사용할 수 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 잘 타지 못했다: 'soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well'이므로 꽤 잘 탔음. 불일치
❌ ① 자전거 대여 서비스: 'has a bike rental service' 원문 일치
❌ ② Dan의 설득: 'Dan persuaded me to try one' 원문 일치
❌ ④ 걸작 같았다: 'like a masterpiece painted by Mother Nature' 원문 일치
det.tip: 'pretty well(꽤 잘)'을 놓치면 오답. 부정/긍정 판단 시 부사에 주의

questions.passage: Fisherman's Wharf is popular for its pretty shops and seafood restaurants. ①We were hungry, but it took almost an hour for us to look around and decide what to eat for lunch. ②We chose to eat a roasted crab and clam chowder soup. ③The sea lions peacefully lied on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate. ④They didn't smell pleasant up close, yet their cuteness delayed our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 문장을 고르시오.

det.korean: 바다사자들이 부두 근처 부표 위에 평화롭게 누워있는(lying) 모습이 녹는 초콜릿 같았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ lied → lying: 'sea lions lying on the floats'에서 lying은 현재분사로 sea lions를 수식. lie(눕다)의 현재분사는 lying. lied는 lie(거짓말하다)의 과거형
❌ ① 정상: 'it took + 시간 + for + 목적격 + to부정사' 구문
❌ ② 정상: chose to eat 구조
❌ ④ 정상: smell + 형용사(pleasant), yet 등위접속사
det.tip: lie 변화: lie-lay-lain(눕다) / lie-lied-lied(거짓말하다). lying은 두 동사 모두의 현재분사이지만, lied는 '거짓말했다'의 과거형

questions.passage: I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us aboard, and we were off.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

케이블카가 휠체어 사용자를 수용하지 않아서 글쓴이는 (          )했다.

det.korean: 케이블카가 휠체어를 수용하지 않는다는 것을 알고 실망했다(disappointed).
det.analysis: ✅ disappointed: 'I was disappointed to find out that~'에서 감정을 나타내는 핵심 단어
det.tip: disappointed(실망한) — be disappointed to V: ~해서 실망하다. 패러프레이징된 한국어 문장에서 원문 단어를 찾아야 함

questions.passage: Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, yelling and waving. After turning me around, Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came. Dan said, "I guess it's time to leave now." That wasn't a problem because I had gotten my picture! Another memorable part of the trip was the bike ride. Dan found out that the National Park has a bike rental service and offers hand-crank bikes. Dan __________ me to try one. (persuasion)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: Dan이 나에게 하나를 타보라고 설득했다(persuaded).
det.analysis:
✅ persuaded: 과거시제 문맥(found out, had 등)에 맞게 persuasion(명사) → persuade(동사) → persuaded(과거형)
❌ persuasion: 명사는 동사 자리에 올 수 없음
❌ persuading: 진행형/분사로는 문장 구조 불완전
det.tip: persuasion(명사, 설득) → persuade(동사) → persuaded(과거형). 'Dan + 동사 + me to try' 구조에서 동사 과거형 필요

questions.passage: While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped frequently to appreciate the fresh air blowing through the giant sequoias. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, which is about 63.7 meters tall and is almost 3,000 years old. __________
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ it / massive / was / and / I / felt / quite / small / in / comparison ]
questions.wa: It was massive, and I felt quite small in comparison.
accept: It was massive, and I felt quite small in comparison.
it was massive, and i felt quite small in comparison.
It was massive, and I felt quite small in comparison
it was massive, and i felt quite small in comparison

det.korean: 그것은 거대했고(massive), 비교하면(in comparison) 나는 꽤 작게(quite small) 느꼈다.
det.analysis: ✅ 'It was massive, and I felt quite small in comparison.' — 원문 문장 그대로. 주어+be동사+형용사, and 접속사, 주어+동사+부사+형용사+전치사구
det.tip: 10단어 배열. 'in comparison'(비교하면)이 문장 끝에 위치. quite는 small을 수식하는 부사

questions.ans: It was massive, and I felt quite small in comparison.

questions.passage: I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, including one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was fortunate to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was courage. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 장애물과 도전이 있었지만, 용기(courage)만 있으면 된다는 메시지.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 도전과 용기로 가득한 여행의 의미: 글 전체를 관통하는 주제. obstacles, challenges, courage, new world
❌ ① 관광 명소 소개: 부분적 내용일 뿐 주제가 아님
❌ ② 여행 가이드: 정보 전달이 아닌 경험과 교훈의 글
❌ ③ 곰 대처법: 하나의 에피소드일 뿐 글 전체 주제가 아님
det.tip: 마지막 문단이 글의 주제를 요약. 'All I needed was courage' + 'looking forward to my next trip'

questions.passage: A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars do not accommodate wheelchair users. Fisherman's Wharf, Yosemite National Park, encountering a black bear, and riding hand-crank bikes were all part of this journey. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? All I needed to take with me was courage.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요약문으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 글쓴이는 샌프란시스코에서 부모님과 함께 편안한 여행을 즐겼다.
휠체어를 탄 글쓴이가 친구와 함께 용기를 갖고 다양한 도전을 극복한 여행기이다.
글쓴이는 요세미티에서 곰에게 공격당해 여행을 중단했다.
샌프란시스코의 대중교통은 장애인에게 완벽하게 접근 가능하다.

det.korean: 휠체어 사용자인 글쓴이가 용기(courage)로 도전을 극복한 여행기.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 글 전체를 정확히 요약: 휠체어+친구+도전+용기
❌ ① 부모님 없이 갔고, 편안하지만은 않았음(곰 만남, 케이블카 불가 등)
❌ ③ 곰에게 공격당하지 않았고 여행은 계속됨
❌ ④ 케이블카가 휠체어 불가였으므로 '완벽'은 틀림
det.tip: 요약문은 글 전체를 대표해야 함. 부분적 에피소드가 아닌 전체 흐름과 주제를 담은 선지를 선택

questions.stem:
다음 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.

[조건]
1. "나는 장애물을 극복하고 도전에 맞서기 위해 용기가 필요했다."를 영어로 쓰시오.
2. 반드시 overcome, challenges, courage를 포함할 것.
3. 10단어 이상으로 쓸 것.
questions.wa: I needed courage to overcome obstacles and meet challenges.
accept: I needed courage to overcome obstacles and meet challenges.
I needed courage to overcome obstacles and meet challenges

det.korean: 나는 장애물을 극복하고 도전에 맞서기 위해 용기(courage)가 필요했다.
det.analysis:
✅ 'I needed courage to overcome obstacles and meet challenges.' — 원문 맥락 기반 영작
- overcome obstacles(장애물을 극복하다) + meet/face challenges(도전에 맞서다)
- courage(용기)를 필수 포함
det.tip: overcome obstacles(장애물 극복), meet/face challenges(도전에 맞서다), courage(용기) — 글의 핵심 메시지를 담은 문장

questions.ans: I needed courage to overcome obstacles and meet challenges.
